drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Counsel: Enclosed is our proposed response to Plaintiff’s First Requests for Production. edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff’s First Requests for Production as follows. These responses are subject to the applicable rules of civil procedure and any governing court orders.

1. PRIVILEGE AND PROTECTION. Defendant will not produce materials protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, or other applicable protection. Any withholding on these grounds will be identified in the applicable request-specific response and described as required by the governing rules and court orders.

2. PRODUCTION. Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control following a reasonable search, subject to specific objections stated in its request-by-request responses. The parties should confer regarding production timing, format, and any disputed scope.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent responsive documents are withheld on privilege or protection grounds, Defendant will provide a privilege log as required by the applicable rules and court orders or as otherwise agreed by the parties.
4. SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will supplement or correct these responses as required by the applicable rules and court orders.

Internal review: Before service, add request-by-request responses, confirm the search and production status, specify any objections and whether responsive materials are being withheld, and establish applicable production deadlines. Confirm whether a privilege log is required and available. This general response alone should not be treated as a complete response to the requests.

edits.text: Defendant's Response to Requests for Production — INTERNAL DRAFT; NOT FOR SERVICE

PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. These general provisions must accompany complete request-by-request responses and do not independently constitute Defendant’s responses to Plaintiff’s First Requests for Production. This draft is not ready for service. Final responses must comply with the applicable rules of civil procedure and governing court orders.

2. REQUEST-SPECIFIC RESPONSES AND PRODUCTION. Each response must identify the request, state any specific objection and its grounds, and state whether responsive materials are being withheld on the basis of that objection. Each response must accurately describe the search and production status and identify the scope of production, including any limitations. Responsive, non-privileged documents within Defendant’s possession, custody, or control will be produced following a reasonable search in accordance with applicable deadlines. Firm production dates, including any rolling-production completion date, must be confirmed and included before service. Proposed discussions do not themselves extend any deadline.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. Any request-specific withholding on grounds of privilege or protection must be expressly identified. Defendant will describe withheld materials as required by the governing rules and court orders, with sufficient information to permit assessment of the asserted protection without revealing protected information. Defendant proposes conferring promptly regarding log format, timing, and any permissible agreed exclusions. No proposed logging arrangement alters existing obligations absent agreement or court order as applicable.

SERVICE HOLD: Obtain the full requests and confirm the response deadline and governing orders. Add a separate response for every request; verify objections, withholding, custodians and sources searched or remaining, search status, production status, and firm production dates with the client and collection team. Do not represent that searches or productions are complete without verification. If additional time is necessary, obtain an effective extension or appropriate relief rather than assume a conference suspends deadlines.

Before service, verify whether privileged responsive materials have been withheld, the applicable logging requirements, and a supportable log delivery date. Any agreed exclusions or alternative logging procedure must be consistent with governing rules and orders.

No confidential severance figure appears in the supplied text, and no hidden-content categories are identified for removal. Block this package pending completion and authorization for external transmission; the cover correspondence may be reviewed separately.
